finalText:
# NIST SP 800-63B-4: password requirements for verifiers and CSPs

The current revision is **SP 800-63B-4**, dated 26 Aug 2025. The superseded Rev. 3 page says: "This revision of NIST SP 800-63 has been superseded by NIST SP 800-63-4 as of August 1, 2025." (https://pages.nist.gov/800-63-3/sp800-63b.html). The Rev. 4 page states: "This publication supersedes NIST Special Publication (SP) 800-63B." (https://pages.nist.gov/800-63-4/sp800-63b.html). All quotes below come from the password sections (3.1.1.1–3.1.1.2) of https://pages.nist.gov/800-63-4/sp800-63b.html.

| Topic | Keyword | Value |
|---|---|---|
| Single-factor minimum length | SHALL | 15 characters |
| Maximum length | SHOULD (permit at least) | 64 characters |
| Composition rules | SHALL NOT | — |
| Periodic change | SHALL NOT | — |
| Password hints | SHALL NOT | — |
| Security questions / KBA | SHALL NOT | — |
| Blocklist check | SHALL | — |
| Password managers / autofill | SHALL (allow) | — |
| Salt length | SHALL (at least) | 32 bits |
| SP 800-132 hashing scheme | SHOULD | — |

**Notes on specific rules:**
- **Maximum length:** 64 is a minimum for the maximum length that verifiers allow. It is not a cap on password length.
- **Shorter passwords in multi-factor use:** Passwords used only as part of multi-factor authentication may be shorter, but not below 8 characters.
- **Forced changes:** Even though periodic changes are forbidden, verifiers SHALL force a change when there is evidence of compromise.
- **Paste:** Allowing "paste" is only a SHOULD. Allowing password managers and autofill is a SHALL.
- **Hashing:** Salting and hashing with "a suitable password hashing scheme" is a SHALL. Using an approved scheme from SP 800-132 specifically is only a SHOULD.

**What wasn't checked:**
- No drafts of Rev. 4 were examined.
- I'm not making any claim about how Rev. 3 worded these rules. One worker's recollection of the Rev. 3 wording came from memory, not from a page it opened.
- No worker found any sources that disagreed with each other.
